title: QUIC RFC 9000 Connection ID Retry Sequencing and Migration Pool Tail
purpose: Describe the S5P1P1 tail closure for non-sequenced client-selected and Retry connection IDs plus migration-aware local CID replenishment.
design_summary: Peer connection-ID sequence state records the peer Initial Source Connection ID as the implicit sequence-0 value when that value has been observed, rather than using transient client-selected or Retry-provided destination connection IDs. NEW_CONNECTION_ID and preferred_address connection-ID admission share this sequencing input so a Retry Source Connection ID can later be explicitly issued as sequence 1 or higher. Local CID issuance continues to replenish the peer-usable pool when a packet arrives on a previously unused locally issued CID, including migrated-path packets, while respecting the peer active_connection_id_limit, zero-length local CID mode, and local issuance budget.
data_and_state_considerations: The observed peer Initial Source CID remains a copied runtime field and is exposed only as a read-only span at the sequencing boundary. The first client-selected Destination CID and the Retry Source CID remain packet-routing or packet-protection inputs unless later received through an explicit peer-issued CID surface. Locally issued CID route and stateless-reset-token state remain paired so replacement NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames advertise the exact bytes and token registered with the endpoint.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A first client-selected Destination CID can later be accepted as an explicitly sequenced peer-issued CID without colliding with sequence 0.
A maximum-length Retry Source CID can later be accepted through preferred_address sequence 1 after the peer Initial Source CID is observed.
A preferred_address CID equal to the observed peer Initial Source CID remains invalid because the Initial Source CID owns sequence 0.
Migration-path replenishment is suppressed when the peer active_connection_id_limit is already full or local CID issuance budget is exhausted.
risks: This slice does not add a public local migration initiation API.
This slice does not change Retry integrity validation or Retry packet authentication behavior.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the remaining S5P1P1 generated trace tail only. It does not claim multipath, public migration controls, Retry integrity changes, public API widening, or hosted interop readiness.
